# NUMBER-PARSE-PATTERN v1.2 routes: which implementation decides each literal shape of Double.parseDouble / Float.parseFloat in java.base.
# route M3 = the absorbed FastDoubleParser atoms decide; route JDK = the original FloatingDecimal converter decides (the M3 atom declines:
# a hex kernel returns NaN, so valueOfHexLiteral calls FloatingDecimal.readJavaFormatString; a decimal literal whose exponent number
# reached the clamp reaches the decimal kernel with DECLINED_EXPONENT, so it returns NaN and valueOfFloatLiteral calls
# FloatingDecimal.readJavaFormatString; a grammar rejection throws and the wiring catches IllegalArgumentException). Line numbers of the
# HEX_* rows name the pre-image bf16b786637 (atoms and hashes: HEX_ATOMS.tsv); those of the DEC_* rows name the pre-image cdd1098fc05f

column3: hex literal whose significand the parser holds exactly (not truncated) and below 2^63, exponent number below the clamp, power within [MIN_EXPONENT, MAX_EXPONENT] (every Double/Float.toHexString output)
column5: HEX_ROUTE v1: HEX_LITERALS_TO_FLOATING_DECIMAL = true in both kernels
column6: RESIDUE: the donor body rounds this shape once and correctly, but the kernel receives the parser's power and cannot tell this shape from HEX_EXPONENT_CLAMP; serving it on M3 again needs an exact exponent from parseHexFloatLiteral (candidate HEX_EXACT_M3, a later leaf, same gates)
column7: hex differential categories 0/1 (toHexString) identical on the post-image; bench in PERF.tsv

column3: unsigned significand >= 2^63: 16 significant hex digits with a leading digit 8-f, or such a 16-digit prefix kept by the re-parse
column6: RESIDUE (anti-pattern): (double) significand + (significand < 0 ? 2^64 : 0) rounds the signed value s - 2^64 (63-bit magnitude: 10 bits dropped for a double, 39 for a float), then rounds again after + 2^64 (11 / 40 bits); 0x8Db1Ffd473B83a5fp196: the cast leaves 0x8db1ffd473b83c00, a false halfway point, round-half-even gives ...4000 (bits 0x5021b63ffa8e7708) instead of ...3800 (stock 0x5021b63ffa8e7707). One rounding needs a sticky shift: (double) ((s >>> 1) | (s & 1)) * 2
column7: jackson-fdp corpus: 1,207 double + 96 float literals (hex_defect_model.py model: 7,854 of 7,854 difference rows reproduced); generated DOUBLE_BIT63 / FLOAT_BIT63 shapes: 1,585 / 1,279 pre-image differences

column3: digitCount > 16 and the re-parse dropped digits (it keeps 15 or 16 hex digits)
column6: RESIDUE (anti-pattern): the dropped digits reach the kernel only as isSignificandTruncated, which selects the exponent and nothing else: no sticky bit, so a kept halfway pattern with non-zero dropped digits rounds to even instead of up. A sticky flag (any non-zero dropped digit ORed into the kept significand's last bit) would make one rounding correct
column7: jackson-fdp corpus: 6 double literals; generated DOUBLE_TRUNCATED_STICKY / FLOAT_TRUNCATED_STICKY shapes: 587 / 451 pre-image differences

column3: exponent number with a digit beyond the clamp (MAX_EXPONENT_NUMBER 1024: 10240 parses as 1024, 100000 as 10000) and fraction digits that bring clamp - 4 x fraction digits into range
column6: RESIDUE (anti-pattern): the exponent number stops growing at 1024 and the fraction adjustment is added afterwards, so 0x.1p10240 gives 2^1020 (0x7fb0000000000000) instead of Infinity, and 0x0.<2500 zeros>1p100000 gives 0.0625; an exact route needs an exponent that saturates only after the adjustment
column7: not in the jackson-fdp corpus (binary exponents < 1100); hex differential category 5: 35,194 double / 4,269 float pre-image differences of 50,000; generated CLAMPED shape: 3,003 / 1,585

column3: every decimal literal without an exponent or with an exponent number below MAX_EXPONENT_NUMBER (1024)
column5: PR #2215; DEC_EXPONENT_CLAMP v1 changed only the two parseDecFloatLiteral templates, and in them only a decline block before the kernel call (DEC_BYTECODE_METHOD_DELTA.tsv: every other method of the 24 classes instruction-identical)
column7: M3ParseDifferential diff 600000 sha256 233e0f59... on stock, pre-image and post-image; decimal differential (DEC_DIFFERENTIAL v1) category GENERAL identical on pre-image and post-image; verifier corpus seed 0x5EED2245 (200,000 decimal literals) identical to stock; PERF_GATE_DEC.tsv

column3: decimal literal whose exponent number reaches MAX_EXPONENT_NUMBER: the exponent loop stops multiplying at 1024 (10240 parses as 1024, 100000 as 10000, 2147483648 as 2147), and the digit counts are added afterwards, in both directions: fraction digits ("0." + 723 zeros + "1e10240", "0." + 9999 zeros + "1e100000") and integer digits beyond the 19 the re-parse keeps ("1" + 1100 zeros + "e-10240", "1" + 800 zeros + "e-10240"); also every exponent number of 1024 to 10239 that was not clamped
column5: DEC_EXPONENT_CLAMP v1: parseDecFloatLiteral passes DECLINED_EXPONENT (Integer.MIN_VALUE) as both exponents, outside the decimal range of both kernels, so the kernel declines and valueOfFloatLiteral calls FloatingDecimal.readJavaFormatString; an exponent number of 1024 to 10239 that was not clamped already lies outside the kernel range unless about 700 or more digits bring it back, so declining it too costs nothing
column6: RESIDUE (anti-pattern, fixed by routing): a saturating accumulator feeds a later adjustment, so the adjustment can bring a saturated value back into range; M3 gave 1e300 (0x7e37e43c8800759c), 1.0 (0x3ff0000000000000), 1e76 (0x4fb61bcca7119916) and about 1e-224 where the JDK gives Infinity, Infinity, 0.0 and 0.0. An exact M3 route would accumulate the exponent number past the clamp and saturate after the digit counts (candidate DEC_EXACT_M3; not needed, the shape is rare)
